Done. `transcribeOpenAi` (shared by the OpenAI and Groq engines) now clamps the prompt to the last `OPENAI_PROMPT_LIMIT = 896` characters before writing the multipart field — the same keep-the-tail rule `buildRecognitionPrompt` uses. Prompts of 896 characters or fewer pass through unchanged. The Gemini path and `host.ts` are untouched.

Changed paths:
- `src/cloud.ts` — exported `OPENAI_PROMPT_LIMIT = 896`, clamped `form.set("prompt", ...)`
- `tests/cloud-prompt.test.ts` — new node:test file stubbing `fetch` to capture the FormData `prompt` field (903-char → last 896 chars; 100-char → unchanged)

Verification: `node --test tests/cloud-prompt.test.ts` → 3/3 pass; `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.

APPROACH: Added `export const OPENAI_PROMPT_LIMIT = 896` above `transcribeOpenAi` in src/cloud.ts and changed the prompt field to `request.prompt.slice(-OPENAI_PROMPT_LIMIT)`, keeping the tail per the existing `buildRecognitionPrompt` convention. Wrote tests/cloud-prompt.test.ts in the repo's node:test style: a fetch stub captures the FormData body and returns `{ text: "ok" }`, then asserts the sent `prompt` for a 903-char input (length 896, equals `prompt.slice(-896)`) and for a 100-char input (exact string). Both contract verification commands exit 0.

LESSON: When a shared OpenAI-compatible function serves two engines, clamping at the single `form.set("prompt", ...)` site covers both callers without touching host.ts prompt construction.
